answer: Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. Based on the information provided, it appears that the SAML login is not functioning correctly, and new starters are not being provisioned automatically. According to our documentation [DOC-AUTH-003], the assertion consumer service URL in your identity provider must match the value shown on the SSO settings page, including the trailing path. Additionally, the NameID in the assertion should be the user's email address in lower case. It's also recommended to enable just-in-time provisioning if new users should be created on first login, and set a default role for provisioned users. Please ensure that the assertion consumer service URL is correctly configured and that just-in-time provisioning is enabled. If the issue persists, please let us know what you observed.
The delay in metrics is expected due to aggregation before being sent [DOC-INT-002].

We appreciate your urgent concern. The application cannot read a variable that appears to be set [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Check the scope at which the variable was defined. Service scope overrides project scope, and project scope overrides organisation defaults [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Store anything sensitive as a secret rather than a variable. Secrets are masked in logs and are not readable through the API after creation [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Review the environment overrides page, which lists values that differ from the defaults for each environment [DOC-DEPLOY-004]. Redeploy after changing configuration. Running containers do not pick up new values without a restart [DOC-DEPLOY-004].

To prevent secrets from appearing in logs, store them as secrets rather than variables. Secrets are masked in logs and are not readable through the API after creation. We've identified some common causes of elevated response latency. A large gap between median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page suggests contention or queueing rather than a uniformly slower service [DOC-PERF-001]. Check memory utilisation across instances, as sustained utilisation above eighty per cent typically shows up as latency before it shows up as failure [DOC-PERF-001]. Review the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view to identify whether the time is being spent in your service or waiting on another [DOC-PERF-001].

To roll back a failed release, open the revisions page for the service and identify the last revision that was healthy. Select roll back on that revision. Traffic moves within roughly thirty seconds and no rebuild takes place. If the release included a database migration, roll the migration back before the service, or the older code will encounter a schema it does not expect.

Database connection pool exhaustion is a common issue when the pool size multiplied by the instance count exceeds the database connection limit [DOC-PERF-003]. Connections are not being returned to the pool after use [DOC-PERF-003]. Long-running transactions are holding connections open [DOC-PERF-003]. To resolve this, you can try restoring into a new database instance rather than over the existing one, so the current state is preserved while you verify the restore [DOC-DATA-002]. Allow roughly ten minutes per hundred gigabytes for the restore, and considerably longer where the instance is also under load [DOC-DATA-002].

Requests return 429 Too Many Requests [DOC-API-001]. Limits appear lower than the documented figure [DOC-API-001]. The limit applies per organisation rather than per key [DOC-API-001]. Implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429 responses rather than retrying immediately [DOC-API-001].
Thank you for getting in touch. I could not find documentation that answers this, so a support engineer will look at your ticket and reply directly.
The billing period runs from the anniversary of the subscription date [DOC-BILL-001]. Check the billing period dates at the top of the invoice to confirm this [DOC-BILL-001].

To avoid being throttled and instead pay overage, you should configure alerts at fifty, eighty and ninety-five per cent of allowance rather than relying on the cap as a warning [DOC-BILL-003]. An account owner can also raise the spend cap immediately from the billing page and service will resume within a minute [DOC-BILL-003].

Audit logs are retained for ninety days on Business plans [DOC-SEC-001]. You can export the relevant period to object storage for anything needed beyond the retention window [DOC-SEC-003]. Note that read access to resources is not logged on Business plans, only administrative and configuration changes [DOC-SEC-003]. Audit log exports are themselves audited, including the fields selected and the destination [DOC-SEC-003].

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. Based on the information provided, it's possible that the issue with your webhook endpoint is due to a non-2xx status being returned by the endpoint, which is causing the delivery to be retried. According to our documentation, failed deliveries are retried with backoff for twenty-four hours, after which the endpoint is disabled and the account is notified [DOC-API-003]. To resolve the issue, we recommend checking the webhook delivery log, which records every attempt with the response status and body for the last seven days [DOC-API-003]. We also suggest returning a 2xx status as quickly as possible and processing the event asynchronously, as deliveries time out after five seconds [DOC-API-003].

We've seen cases where the assertion consumer service URL in the identity provider doesn't match the value shown on the SSO settings page, including the trailing path [DOC-AUTH-003]. It's also possible that the NameID is not the user's email address in lower case, or that just-in-time provisioning is disabled on the connection [DOC-AUTH-003].

Audit logs are retained for ninety days on Business plans [DOC-SEC-001]. Filter the audit log by actor, resource and date range [DOC-SEC-003]. Configure continuous export to your own storage if a policy requires retention longer than the plan provides [DOC-SEC-003]. Note that read access to resources is not logged on Business plans, only administrative and configuration changes [DOC-SEC-003].

The issue may be due to the role being granted at project scope rather than organisation scope [DOC-ACCT-001]. To resolve this, check the effective permissions view for the user, which resolves direct roles and group memberships together [DOC-ACCT-001]. Confirm the invitation was accepted, as pending invitations appear in a separate section and expire after seven days [DOC-ACCT-001].

Forwarding pauses after one hour of consecutive failures and must be resumed manually once the destination is healthy [DOC-INT-002]. Check the forwarding status page, which shows the last successful delivery and any error returned by the destination [DOC-INT-002]. Verify the destination credential separately if delivery has stopped entirely, as expired credentials are the most common cause [DOC-INT-002].

The billing period runs from the anniversary of the subscription date [DOC-BILL-001]. You can check the billing period dates at the top of the invoice. Set a usage alert on the billing page so that unexpected accrual is noticed during the period rather than at the end of it [DOC-BILL-001].

We've identified a few potential causes for the increased latency. It's possible that the service is running close to its memory limit and spending time in garbage collection [DOC-PERF-001]. Additionally, a downstream dependency may have slowed and the delay is propagating [DOC-PERF-001]. It's also possible that instance count is not scaling with the load pattern [DOC-PERF-001]. To further diagnose the issue, we recommend comparing median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page to identify whether the time is being spent in your service or waiting on another [DOC-PERF-001].

A spend cap can stop a production workload. Spend caps apply per organisation and cannot currently be set per project. Read the rate limit headers returned with every response . Implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429 responses rather than retrying immediately .
